application_guidance.input_pattern: Convex block-separable composite minimization using exact UCDC updates and a finite initial level-set radius.
read_original_when: Changing sampling, using inexact block solves, changing the radius definition, or transferring to another oracle model.
Seeking strong-convexity or nonuniform-sampling results outside case (i).
sensitive_conditions: Radius is the source's maximum over all minimizers and all initial-sublevel points.
The statement is an iteration guarantee for this algorithm; exact block minimization has its own implementation cost.
A theorem budget needs valid gap/radius information; unknown F* is not automatically an available stopping certificate.

complexity_scope.guarantee: For every admissible fixed instance and initialization, success probability at least 1-rho over the block draws.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: None in the displayed threshold: C=2n max{R_L(x0)^2,Delta0}; +2 and -C/Delta0 are retained. Norm geometry and Li enter through R_L.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact selected-block gradient and exact selected-block quadratic-proximal minimization.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Last iterate x_k; objective gap F(x_k)-F*.
complexity_scope.regime: The complete assumptions and parameter domains in statement; finite radius over all initial-sublevel points and all minimizers.
complexity_scope.resource: k selected-block gradient evaluations and k exact block minimizations; sampling, block arithmetic, preprocessing and cost of implementing minimization are separate. No full gradient or repeated objective evaluation is required by the fixed-budget update.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Selected UCDC Algorithm 2; no coverage of arbitrary algorithms or Oracle Complexity lower bounds.

content.intended_use: Select an iteration budget for a last-iterate convex composite objective-gap guarantee.

proofs.locator: §2, PDF pp.8–9, Theorem 1(i), Eqs.(13),(16)–(20); §3, PDF pp.10–11, Lemma 2, Eqs.(21)–(24); §3.1, PDF pp.11–12, Lemma 3 and Theorem 4(i), Eqs.(25)–(29).
map: PDF pp.7,10–11: Eq.(8) bounds a selected-block update by its majorant. Uniform averaging and separability give Lemma 2: E[F(x_{k+1})-F*|x_k] <= (H(x_k,T(x_k))-F*)/n +(n-1)(F(x_k)-F*)/n, where H(x,T)=f(x)+<nabla f(x),T>+||T||_L^2/2+Psi(x+T) and T(x) minimizes H.

PDF p.11: Lemma 3 evaluates H along y=alpha x*+(1-alpha)x. Convexity gives the scalar upper bound F(x)-alpha(F(x)-F*)+alpha^2||x-x*||_L^2/2. Minimizing over alpha in [0,1] yields Eq.(25), with alpha=min{1,(F(x)-F*)/||x-x*||_L^2} when the denominator is positive.

PDF p.12: Descent keeps iterates in the initial sublevel set. Thus ||x_k-x*||_L<=R_L(x0). Combining Lemma 2 and Lemma 3 gives Eq.(29): conditional expected gap <=max{1-(F(x_k)-F*)/(2n R_L(x0)^2),1-1/(2n)}(F(x_k)-F*), for positive gaps.
PDF p.12: With xi_k=F(x_k)-F*, monotonicity gives 0<=xi_k<=Delta0. Choosing C=2n max{R_L(x0)^2,Delta0} yields E[xi_{k+1}|xi_k]<=xi_k-xi_k^2/C. Theorem 1(i) applies since 0<epsilon<xi_0<C.

PDF pp.8–9: Theorem 1(i) truncates xi_k below epsilon, sets theta_k to the expectation of the truncated variable, and derives theta_{k+1}<=theta_k-theta_k^2/C and theta_{k+1}<=(1-epsilon/C)theta_k. The first recurrence reaches theta<=epsilon within the reciprocal-drift phase; the second reaches theta<=epsilon rho in the geometric phase. The +2 in Eq.(13) accommodates integer phase budgets. Markov's inequality gives the claimed probability and Eq.(27).

assumptions: f:R^N->R is differentiable convex. For every x in R^N, t in R^Ni and block i, ||nabla_i f(x+Ui t)-nabla_i f(x)||*_(i)<=Li||t||_(i), with Li>0.
Psi=sum_i Psi_i is block separable proper closed convex extended-real-valued; the exact block quadratic-proximal subproblems are used.
X* is nonempty, F*>-infinity, x0 belongs to dom Psi, and R_L(x0) is finite.
The positive initial gap satisfies 0<epsilon<Delta0; 0<rho<1. Sampling has conditional probability 1/n for every block at every step.
statement.conclusion: Let C=2n max{R_L(x0)^2,Delta0}. If k >= (C/epsilon)(1+log(1/rho))+2-C/Delta0, then P(F(x_k)-F*<=epsilon)>=1-rho. This is case (i), Eq.(27), of Theorem 4.
statement.objects_and_definitions: F(x)=f(x)+Psi(x), x in R^N. U=[U1,...,Un] is a column permutation of I_N, Ui has Ni columns, sum Ni=N and x^(i)=Ui^T x. Bi is positive definite, ||t||_(i)^2=<Bi t,t>, and ||s||*_(i)^2=<Bi^(-1)s,s>. Define ||x||_L^2=sum_i Li||x^(i)||_(i)^2, X*=argmin F, F*=min F, Delta0=F(x0)-F*. The source's radius is R_L(x0)=max_y max_{x* in X*}{||y-x*||_L : F(y)<=F(x0)}. It ranges over every minimizer, not a nearest-minimizer distance. x_k is the kth UCDC iterate: choose i conditionally uniformly each step, compute the exact minimizer h of <nabla_i f(x_k),t>+(Li/2)||t||_(i)^2+Psi_i(x_k^(i)+t), and set x_{k+1}=x_k+Ui h.
statement.parameter_domains: N,n,Ni are positive integers, sum Ni=N; Bi are positive definite; Li>0; 0<epsilon<Delta0<infinity; rho in (0,1); R_L(x0)<infinity; k is a nonnegative integer. log is the natural logarithm.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every objective, block geometry and deterministic initialization satisfying these assumptions, for every admissible epsilon and rho, and every nonnegative integer k satisfying the displayed threshold, the probability is over the UCDC block draws for that instance.
